text: Debugging is a crucial skill for any programmer, and having a clear strategy makes it much less stressful. First, you must identify the bug by reproducing the problem and understanding what the code was supposed to do. Instead of guessing, use a systematic approach: check your latest changes, read error messages carefully, and isolate small sections of code. Debugging tools, like breakpoints in an IDE, are invaluable for pausing the program and inspecting variable values. Additionally, adding temporary logging statements can reveal the program's flow and data at specific points. By combining these tools with a patient, methodical mindset, you can quickly pinpoint the root cause and move on to creating a reliable fix.
